originalGroup.material:
Animal Shelter Blankets 015

Our school collected blankets for an animal shelter. The shelter asked for clean, washable blankets with no loose threads. Some families brought thick quilts. They looked warm, but the shelter’s washing machine was too small for them. Volunteers checked each donation against the list instead of judging only by appearance. Suitable blankets went into blue boxes. Other items were returned politely with an explanation or passed to a different charity after the donor agreed. The school’s report counted accepted blankets separately from the total number of items brought in. This prevented the collection total from suggesting that every donation had reached the shelter.

Our school collected blankets for an animal shelter. The shelter asked for clean, washable blankets with no loose threads. Some families brought thick quilts. They looked warm, but the shelter’s washing machine was too small for them. Volunteers checked each donation against the list instead of judging only by appearance. Suitable blankets went into blue boxes. Other items were returned politely with an explanation or passed to a different charity after the donor agreed. The school’s report counted accepted blankets separately from the total number of items brought in. This prevented the collection total from suggesting that every donation had reached the shelter.
questions.explanation: B正确：厚被机容量不够；A把看着暖当全适用。

originalGroup.material:
School Bird Count Window 015

For a bird-count project, pupils observed the same playground tree for ten minutes at lunch each day. They wrote down birds they could clearly identify. On Wednesday, a heavy shower kept everyone indoors. One member entered zero in the table because no birds had been written down. Another pointed out that zero could mean someone had looked and seen no birds. On Wednesday, no observation had been made at all.
The team changed that cell to "not observed" and explained the rain. On Friday, they did watch the tree for ten minutes and saw no birds, so zero remained correct for that day. The report kept these two cases separate. Members also noted that they could count only visible birds during the chosen minutes. Their figures did not show every bird that used the tree at other times.

originalGroup.material:
Drama Subtitle Revision 015

The drama club added English subtitles to a short film. A speech tool produced the first draft. It turned the character’s line "Wait by the gate" into "Wait by the lake." The sentence still sounded sensible, so a quick spelling check did not catch it. Two pupils compared the subtitles with the recorded speech and the script. They corrected the place name and several speaker labels.
Another line was not clear in the recording, and the script had changed during filming. The club asked the actor what had been said instead of guessing from the tool’s output. After checking, they kept a note of the correction. The final credits thanked the pupil reviewers as well as naming the software used. The club said that a fluent-looking draft still needed checking against the actual work.
